text:
Ava (Design): Pushed a tiny prototype for a 'Notify simulation' mode to the preview panel. Figured it might help teams understand who will actually get notified when suppressions, overrides and fallbacks interact. link: https://figma.redwood/notify-sim (screenshot attached) Sam (PM): Nice — love the idea. Does the simulation account for per-channel rate limits and canaries? :eyes: Ravi (Frontend): It shows channel list + why each channel would/ wouldn't fire. Collapsed by default, expands per-channel details. Thinking of adding a 1-line reason: `suppressed by quiet window`, `overridden to pager`, `fallback to email`. Marta (Eng-Accessibility): Important: screen readers need to be told when the simulation finishes so folks using VO get the result. We should use an `aria-live` polite region and a visible summary. Also keyboard nav needs clear focus order — preview open -> simulation button -> results list. Gabe (SRE): Also call out when the policy used in sim is stale vs live config. If someone is testing a canary rollout, they expect to see the live route. Add a small badge: `sim uses snapshot from {time}`. Ava (Design): Good points. Proposal: add a `Simulation details` pill with timestamp, and an `Explain why` expand per-channel. Sketch: (1) Simulation button = `Run notify simulation` (2) Lightweight spinner, then summary banner: "2 channels would notify; 1 suppressed" (3) Expandable rows with reasons. Sam (PM): Copy tweak: instead of "would notify" use "would be notified" — reads better. Also the banner should link to the route used for the sim. Ravi (Frontend): Small CSS thing: use `role="region" aria-labelledby="sim-results-header"` on the results container, then each row can be a `button` for keyboard expand/collapse. Example snippet: ```html

Simulation results

``` Marta (Eng-Accessibility): That looks fine, but make sure the expanded content has `aria-hidden` toggled or moved offscreen for SRs. Also announce counts using clear language: "Simulation complete. Two channels are eligible to receive notifications; one channel is suppressed." Avoid passive voice. Gabe (SRE): Edge case: suppressed channel might still consume quota if it was queued earlier. Can we show "suppression reason + last matched event" so engineers can validate? Also helpful to display which fallback model was chosen (e.g., email fallback after 3 failures). Ava (Design): Agree. New row payload idea (compact): `Channel • state • reason • last_event (ago)`. UI mock uses small fine-print for last_event, e.g., "last match: 3m ago". Sam (PM): UX question: if a user reorders channels in their settings, do we preserve that order in sim? My vote: preserve user-set order. If algorithmic sorting is applied for previews, show a tiny `sorted` tag and provide a toggle to view "user order". Ravi (Frontend): Implementation note — we can pass `orderPreference= user|algorithm` to the sim API. Example request payload: ```json {"policyId":"p-123","previewMode":"simulation","orderPreference":"user"} ``` Marta (Eng-Accessibility): Also note color contrast on the suppressed badge is low in the mock (light gray on pale bg). Increase contrast or add iconography so it doesn't rely only on color. Ava (Design): Good catch — I'll bump contrast and add a small muted icon for suppressed. Copy change per Sam: banner -> "Simulation complete — 2 channels would be notified; 1 is suppressed." Gabe (SRE): One more: include an explanation of automatic fallbacks in the banner only when a fallback was triggered in the sim. Example: "Fallback to email applied for Pager duty after rate limit." Keep the banner terse but link to full log for debugging. notifier-bot: (simulation) Simulation run complete for policy p-123 at 2024-05-12T16:42:10Z — 2 notified, 1 suppressed, 0 failed. Ava (Design): Updated Figma with a11y fixes and the new banner copy. Would love a quick pass from @Marta and @Ravi on the keyboard flow before I hand off to eng. :thumbsup: Marta (Eng-Accessibility): Will do a quick pass today, focusing on aria-live text and contrast. Ravi (Frontend): I'll spike the small API changes and wire up the region + button pattern. Will post a short PR with notes. Sam (PM): This feels like a good incremental win. Thanks all — aim to ship as opt-in toggle in next sprint.
